{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-me8y.30","title":"compress/decompress use u128 for field values, limiting extensibility","description":"## Location
- /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/compress.rs lines 247, 314

## Problem
```rust
pub fn compress(rule: &Rule, field_values: &[u128], out: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, SchcError>
pub fn decompress(rule: &Rule, data: &[u8], out: &mut [u128]) -> Result<(usize, usize), SchcError>
```

Field values are passed as `u128`. This works for most SCHC use cases (IPv6 addresses are 128 bits), but:

1. Cannot represent variable-length fields exceeding 128 bits
2. Wastes memory for small fields (most are 8-32 bits)
3. Cannot represent non-integer field values (e.g., opaque byte sequences)

## API Risk
If SCHC is extended to handle fields larger than 128 bits, or if callers need to compress arbitrary byte sequences as fields, the API would need breaking changes.

## Suggested Fix
Consider a more flexible field value type:
```rust
pub enum FieldValue<'a> {
    Small(u128),
    Large(&'a [u8]),
}
```

Or accept `&[u8]` slices with length validation against `FieldDescriptor::length_bits`.
